Named profiles keep separate cookies, site data, Favorites, history, downloads, and remembered permissions. Device settings and Patron status stay shared; Sync belongs to Personal only.

Changes take effect after restarting Blanc. uBlock Origin protects regular tabs. Blanc’s browser engine can load uBO only in saved sessions, so private sessions stay in memory and use Blanc Blocker. Each provider keeps separate site settings.

Filter lists update automatically. Executable resources update with Blanc releases; custom resource URLs and cloud storage are unavailable. Turning blocking off removes cosmetic CSS; reload a page to undo changes already made by scriptlets.
Stops ads and the hidden trackers that follow you from site to site. On by default.
Sites listed here load with ad-blocking turned off, e.g. for sites that break under it.
Standard limits calls to your default network route. If a call stutters or won\'t connect, try Compatibility; it can reveal local network addresses to the site. Strict is for application-proxy users.
Compatibility — widest call support, less IP privacy
Strict — stronger for proxy users, but can break some video calls

Automatic keeps conversation delay as low as possible. Stable targets about 400 ms of receive buffering. Resilient targets about 1 second for severe crackling or chopped speech, making back-and-forth conversation slower. Start a new call after changing it.
Stable — smoother playback, about 400 ms buffer
Resilient — high stability, about 1 second buffer

Encrypts the behind-the-scenes lookups that turn a web address into a connection, so someone sniffing those lookups can\'t read the names. It does not hide the sites you visit from your network, and it makes the DNS provider someone you trust. Automatic uses encryption when it can and may fall back to ordinary DNS — safe to leave on. If a Wi-Fi login page won\'t load, switch to Automatic or Off temporarily.
Off — use your system setting (best with a VPN)
Quad9 — also blocks known malware sites
The secure DNS address your provider gave you (an https:// link), e.g. https://dns.nextdns.io/<profile>.

Counts active users and which start-page layouts and local features get used. Sends a random install and session id, app version, platform, architecture, coarse OS major, and fixed feature names; never URLs, searches, page content, or private-tab activity. This is pseudonymous measurement sent to a Blanc-owned Cloudflare collector. It stores a keyed hash of the install id; an optional Google Analytics mirror receives that hash and the same limited fields. Turn this off to stop future events.
Removes cookies, cache, and site data for every site. You\'ll be logged out of everything.
Facts checked on this device. Opening this section makes no network request.

Blanc keeps a local, 50-event crash ledger with timestamps, process type, and failure reason. It never includes URLs, page titles, history, profile names, account data, identifiers, quiet-tab state, or closed-tab state, and nothing is sent automatically.

Blanc Patron is how you support Blanc’s development. Every feature, including Blanc Spaces, is free for everyone. A one-time founding license activates once, with no further contact. A monthly or annual subscription checks in with Polar about once a day — your license key and activation id only, never browsing data — to confirm it’s still active.
Already a Patron? Enter the license key available under Purchases in Polar to activate this device.
Blanc uses Chromium through Electron to render websites. Updates to Electron and Chromium arrive with new Blanc releases and replace the whole app. Applying an update requires restarting Blanc.
You can browse Chrome Web Store pages, but Blanc cannot install Chrome extensions.
On macOS, Windows and Linux, Blanc offers explicit login fill from the installed 1Password app. This integration does not save passwords or fill automatically.

Blanc connects to websites you open and GitHub for app updates. Searches and enabled suggestions go to your selected search provider; DNS lookups use your system or selected DNS provider. Selecting Google sends searches and eligible suggestion prefixes to Google.

Enabled usage measurement goes to a Blanc-owned Cloudflare collector and, when configured, its Google Analytics mirror. Sync, Patron, 1Password and tab handoff make separate connections when configured or requested. This describes behavior; it is not a live network monitor.

Something broken, or working in a way it shouldn’t? Reports go to Blanc’s public issue tracker on GitHub. Saying which version you’re on, which operating system, and what page you were looking at makes a report much faster to act on.
